raw.assessment: The incumbent appears useful under stable assignments: 24 such files had seven-minute median handling. Overall, intended-course coverage was 32/40 (80%) and median handling was 17 minutes, missing both targets. Change-sensitive selection or recognition is plausible, not established. The two renamed-course cases limit an instructor-assignment-only explanation. Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish isolation for the unsampled split-course center. Short job duration cannot explain where replacement delays arise.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for historical weeks may select the wrong courses; renaming may independently cause selection errors or make correct courses hard to recognize.
openings.delta: Separate requested-week membership errors from name-recognition errors before changing export rules.
openings.prediction: Holding intended membership fixed, changing only current instructor assignment will alter exported membership if temporal selection is causal. A rename-only case may preserve membership while changing coordinator judgments.
openings.probe: In private staging with fabricated participants, compare paired unchanged, reassigned and renamed courses against explicit requested-week expectations. Inspect internal course identity separately from unchanged-schema CSV labels. Include a split-course fixture with another center's sentinel participant; reject any leakage. Keep attendance entry active.
assumptions: Internal course identity can be inspected without altering the CSV schema.
Historical assignment data needed for any later repair may be unavailable; inspect before committing implementation.

openings.claim: Does handling time primarily arise from reconciling course expectations, spreadsheet import, or obtaining replacements?
openings.delta: Distinguish active coordinator work from elapsed replacement delay; current logs measure neither task-level effort nor request handling.
openings.prediction: If reconciliation dominates, checking/correction minutes will exceed download/import minutes even with a replacement immediately available. If fulfillment dominates elapsed delay, request-to-job-start or completion-to-access time will exceed execution time.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two short sessions with fabricated exports and representative timetable styles; timestamp checking, correction, download and import separately. Trace staged replacement requests through availability. Allocate both probes within six engineer-days and existing hosting; preserve the documented schema and ordinary attendance entry.
assumptions: Fabricated sessions approximate ordinary work sufficiently to prioritize a bounded change; they cannot establish next-40-export success.

raw.assessment: CSV delivery remains required. Two alternative interface changes could remove coordinator reconciliation or replacement-request dependencies. The observations support investigating these dependencies, not either causal explanation. Feasibility within six engineer-days and the hosting allowance remains unverified.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: bind an export to a center-authorized course-week manifest using stable internal course identities, rather than deriving its scope from current instructor assignments or course names. A shared scope contract could make Monday comparison with a separate schedule unnecessary.
openings.delta: Replace inference from mutable labels and assignments with an explicit scope handoff. Former comparison obligations remain: establish the intended courses and week, resolve renames and splits, detect omissions, and identify who may correct scope. The manifest must also count courses with no attendance rows.
openings.prediction: If mutable identity drives the omissions, fixing scope while varying instructor assignments and names will preserve the intended course set; an incomplete manifest will still fail.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging cases, compare incumbent and manifest exports for assignment changes, renames, and a split. Six coordinators specify intended scope before seeing results. Count omissions, foreign-center rows, and total manifest upkeep plus handling time. Check unchanged CSV imports, concurrent attendance entry, engineering effort, and hosting cost before adoption.
assumptions: Stable identities and week-specific scope can be represented within budget.
Coordinators can establish scope without shifting excessive work upstream.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: expose the existing exporter through an authenticated center/week request interface with a retrievable completion result, so coordinators can obtain replacements without an intermediary request-and-wait cycle.
openings.delta: Remove dependence on operator availability. Preserve its obligations: authorize center scope, validate the requested week and courses, signal failures, and identify the latest completed file. Keep the documented CSV and private delivery; export reads must allow attendance entry.
openings.prediction: Replacement elapsed time should approach execution plus retrieval time. Active handling and course-set accuracy may remain unchanged, which would limit this alternative's contribution to the success measure.
openings.probe: Time a fabricated replacement through both interfaces, separating active handling from waiting. Test forged center requests, simultaneous attendance entry, and bounded repeat requests. Reject the change if authorization, schema, six-day effort, or hosting checks fail; retain the next-40-export outcome test.
assumptions: Existing execution can be safely exposed within budget.
Replacement delay substantially reflects mediation rather than necessary scope correction.

openings.claim: Current assignments may misselect historical courses; renames may affect selection or recognition. Authorized stable-identity course-week manifests might prevent reconciliation.
openings.discriminator: Vary assignments/names independently; compare membership and recognition. Fixed manifests resist changes; incomplete manifests fail.
openings.probe: Compare incumbent/manifest using fabricated unchanged/reassigned/renamed/split cases. Coordinators predeclare scope, including empty courses; inspect identities/CSV labels, omissions, correction authority and foreign-center sentinels. Count upkeep plus handling.
openings.uncertainty: Causality, historical data, stable identities, trustworthy scope and implementation cost unverified.

openings.claim: Reconciliation, import and replacement fulfillment may contribute differently.
openings.probe: Six coordinators, two short sessions each, diverse timetable styles: time checking/correction/download/import and request-to-start/completion-to-access.
openings.uncertainty: Timetable completeness and session realism unknown.

openings.claim: Authenticated self-service replacements may remove intermediary waiting.
openings.discriminator: Waiting shrinks; active effort/accuracy may persist.
openings.probe: Compare paths; validate center/week/course scope, forged/repeated requests, failures and latest completed-file retrieval.
openings.uncertainty: Mediation versus necessary correction; exposure feasibility unverified.

post_distill.decision: Probe before choosing. Preserve private authorized delivery, documented CSV/import and concurrent attendance within six engineer-days/existing hosting; verify mechanism feasibility. Reject leakage; sampled absence excludes split center. Synthetic sessions cannot establish next-40 targets: median handling <=12 minutes, >=95% intended course sets, zero foreign-center records.
